newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Canada stays miner choice despite Bre-X - Friedland.
newsitem.headline: Canada stays miner choice despite Bre-X - Friedland.

text.p: Canada will remain the world capital for mine financing despite its fund raising expertise being paralysed by controversy surrounding one of its brightest proteges, Bre-X Minerals Ltd, leading mine financier Robert Friedland told Reuters this week.

Friedland who was voted Canada's mining developer of the year in 1996, is chairman of Ivanhoe Capital Corporation and shot to fame a few years ago when his former company Diamond Fields unearthed the massive Voisey Bay nickel deposit in Labrador.

The find was sold on to the giant Inco mining group for C$4.6 billion. Last month serious doubts arose about Bre-X's gold deposit at Busang, Indonesia which apparently contained over 71 million ounces of gold.
Shares nose-dived when due diligence drilling on the site by the deposit's developer Freeport-McMoRan Inc Copper revealed substantially less gold than the Bre-X drilling samples.
"The immediate impact of Bre-X has been dramatic on the flow of capital to the junior speculative end of the Canadian industry," said Friedland.
"It is not clear what impact it had on the large producing companies as the 20 percent drop in share prices coincided with the Dow correcting over the past 10 days," he added.

One of Friedland's companies Indochina Goldfields Ltd which raised C$270 million from its first public offering in July last year and was valued at over $1 billion pre-Bre-X was worth only about $800 million after the stock market sell off.
Friedland described the reaction of the Canadian markets as like "a deer caught in the headlights not knowing whether to fight or flee".

"Medium term there is speculation that this is a fraud cut from whole cloth. That is definitely premature. Either its one of the world's largest gold deposits or its a fraud and the truth is probably somewhere in between," he said.
Strathcona -- the independent geological consultants brought in to clear up the Busang issue -- are due to report to the market on their findings on April 29.
"Strathcona has an impeccable technical reputation and will report clear scientific knowledge about the drilling. The financial community can then respond," Friedland said.

However, he noted that the reluctance to place capital was patchy. "Our own company Ivanhoe Capital is raising operating capital to invest in talc deposits in China. The industry is happy to go into something which is not inherently speculative but it has hit the smaller companies like a neutron bomb," he said.

But he was convinced the Canadian financing industry would survive the scare. "Canada will remain the world's capital for mining finance because of its expertise in all important areas. It is a large provider (of capital) to the U.S, economy," he said.
Ivanhoe Capital is involved in minerals, energy, telecommunications and real estate in 46 emerging markets and is headquartered in Singapore.
Increasingly Ivanhoe is moving into energy, oil and gas in Russia, Malaysia, China, Indonesia and Peru. "Energy is very significant and is now about half of our portfolio," Friedland said.
Although mining is becoming a smaller part of Invanhoe's interest, Friedland said he was still "fascinated by the industry and the people in it.
"Where else can you make $500 million in capital overnight?" he said.
Friedland was attending a dinner in Zurich on his way to Moscow and Kazakstan where his companies have oil and gold interests.
